audit.why: Emerald+ 56.34% over 2089 games. Level 1 is even because Sion can only walk at you and charge a cone, and every stage after that is Singed once Fling exists — he has no dash, no gap-closer and the slowest approach in the lane. Both layers and the packet chart give the identical read, so nothing moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] is labelled 'Lvl 2' and reads 'Fling + Mega Adhesive comes online'; whys[1] repeats it. Both abilities cannot exist at level 2. Separately, the mid paragraph writes off Sion's level 6 entirely: 'His Insanity Potion at level 6 adds nothing to his chase threat.'
audit.why: Sion does not have Insanity Potion — that is Singed's own R, and the packet flags the line as a wrong ability name. Sion's level-6 ability is Unstoppable Onslaught, 140/100/60s, and it is the single biggest threat to a Singed in this matchup: a screen-length unstoppable charge that ends in a knockup, against a champion with no dash. The _missing rule for this pair says exactly that — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage. Telling the reader Sion's ult 'adds nothing to his chase threat' is the worst sentence on the page.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].when and .text corrected to Lvl 2-3, whys[1] rewritten, and the mid paragraph rebuilt around Unstoppable Onslaught's 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central claim is that Mega Adhesive's root cancels the Decimating Smash charge — 'the root cancels his charge animation' in mid, 'roots Sion through his own Q charge animation' in whys[1]. It also never mentions that two of Sion's damage sources scale off your max health.
audit.why: Mega Adhesive 'slows and grounds enemies who walk on it'. Nothing in that stops a cast. Fling is the ability that does the work: it 'flings them into the air behind Singed', so he ends up displaced out of his own cone regardless of what happens to the charge — and if he lands in the goo he is rooted on top of it. Attributing the interrupt to the root teaches the wrong button order. Separately, Soul Furnace and Glory in Death both carry percent-health scaling in Riot's text ('bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health'), so a Singed stacking HP is feeding both — the _missing rule flags Sion as bypassing stacking resistances for this reason.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, whys[1], the mid paragraph, report[5].t and wants.foe[2] rewritten. The correct order is now stated: Fling displaces, Mega Adhesive holds.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Decimating Smash with no number.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6s, Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11s, Roar of the Slayer 12/11/10/9/8s and Unstoppable Onslaught 140/100/60s. The 140s at rank 1 is the number that decides whether a proxy lap is safe, and it is nowhere on the page.

edits.before: Level 2 flips the lane. The moment Fling comes online, wait for Sion to begin charging Decimating Smash, then Fling him behind you into a pre-placed Mega Adhesive — the root cancels his charge animation and he sits in your cloud for the full duration, unable to leave. From level 3 onward he is genuinely helpless against your pattern: he has no dash, no reliable peel, and Roar of the Slayer only matters if he can get close enough to use it. At level 4-5 start proxying — Sion cannot chase you into the zone between his tower and base, so you freely deny him minions while double-farming. His Insanity Potion at level 6 adds nothing to his chase threat, while yours turns you into a speed demon he will never catch.
edits.after: Level 2 flips the lane. The moment Fling comes online, wait for Sion to begin charging Decimating Smash, then Fling him — the displacement drops him out of his own cone. From level 3 the goo completes it: land him in Mega Adhesive and he is rooted in your cloud with no dash out, and Decimating Smash is only 10s at rank 1 so the window repeats. Roar of the Slayer matters only if he gets close. At 4-5 proxy between his tower and base where he cannot follow. Do not write off his level 6: Unstoppable Onslaught is 140s at rank 1, it is unstoppable, and it can cut your retreat from most of a screen away — hold Flash for the wall, not for the damage.

edits.before: Insanity Potion's movement and regen make you impossible for Sion to run down — his only hope was catching you and that window is now permanently closed.
edits.after: Insanity Potion's speed and regen make you hard to run down, but Unstoppable Onslaught lands too — 140s at rank 1, unstoppable, and it can cut off your retreat.

notes: I deliberately did not claim that Fling interrupts the Decimating Smash charge, only that it displaces Sion out of his own cone. Riot's Fling text confirms the displacement; whether an airborne effect cancels Sion's charge is not in the kit data and the needsResearch fields are empty, so the copy states the part that is certain. The false 'the root cancels his charge animation' claim is removed either way, because Mega Adhesive only slows and grounds.
